questions.questionText: Based on the line graph showing the estimated number of chipmunks in a state park on April 1 of each year from 1989 to 1999, in which year was the estimated number of chipmunks the greatest?
questions.approach: Find the peak of the line—the single highest point on the graph. Trace directly down to the x-axis to read the year. Don't confuse the peak with the most recent point or the steepest rise.
questions.whyRight: The line graph reaches its highest point at 1994. Every other year shows a lower count.
questions.trapAnalysis: {"A": {"name": "First-Point Trap", "explanation": "1989 is the starting year—students who glance at the leftmost point without finding the peak land here."}, "C": {"name": "Adjacent-Year Trap", "explanation": "1995 is right next to the correct year. Students who misread the x-axis by one year pick this."}, "D": {"name": "Most-Recent Trap", "explanation": "1998 is near the end of the graph. Students who equate 'recent' with 'greatest' land here."}}
questions.patternTip: Line graphs: 'greatest' = find the single highest y-value point, then read the x-value. Don't be fooled by the endpoints or the most recent data.

questions.questionText: A fish swam a distance of 5,104 yards. How far did the fish swim, in miles? (1 mile = 1,760 yards)
questions.approach: Converting from smaller unit (yards) to larger unit (miles): divide. 5,104 ÷ 1,760 ≈ 2.9. If the answer is bigger than 5,104, you multiplied—that's wrong.
questions.trapAnalysis: {"A": {"name": "Inverted Fraction Trap", "explanation": "0.3 comes from 1,760 ÷ 5,104 ≈ 0.34—dividing in the wrong direction."}, "C": {"name": "Subtraction Trap", "explanation": "3,344 ≈ 5,104 − 1,760. No arithmetic basis; comes from adding or subtracting rather than converting."}, "D": {"name": "Multiplication Trap", "explanation": "Multiplying 5,104 × 1,760 yields a much larger number; D represents a smaller multiplication error."}}
questions.patternTip: Smaller unit → larger unit = divide. Yards → miles: divide by 1,760. If the result is larger than the original, you went the wrong way.

questions.questionText: Which expression is equivalent to 12x³ − 5x³?
questions.approach: Like terms: subtract the coefficients (12 − 5 = 7) and keep the variable part unchanged (x³). The exponent does NOT change in addition/subtraction.
questions.whyRight: (12 − 5)x³ = 7x³. Coefficient changes, exponent stays the same.
questions.trapAnalysis: {"A": {"name": "Exponent Addition Trap", "explanation": "7x⁶ subtracts coefficients correctly (7) but adds exponents (3 + 3 = 6). Exponent addition is the rule for MULTIPLICATION, not subtraction."}, "B": {"name": "Add Instead of Subtract Trap", "explanation": "17x³ adds the coefficients (12 + 5 = 17) instead of subtracting. The minus sign between the terms means subtract."}, "D": {"name": "Double Error Trap", "explanation": "17x⁶ adds both the coefficients AND the exponents. Two mistakes at once."}}
questions.patternTip: Combining like terms: coefficients add/subtract. Exponents are FROZEN. Exponents only change in multiplication and division. 12x³ − 5x³ = 7x³ (not 7x⁶).

questions.questionText: What is the solution (x, y) to the system x + y = 18 and 5y = x?
questions.approach: Substitute 5y for x: 5y + y = 18 → 6y = 18 → y = 3. Then x = 5(3) = 15. Verify: 15 + 3 = 18 ✓ and 5(3) = 15 ✓.
questions.whyRight: y = 3, x = 15. Both equations confirmed.
questions.trapAnalysis: {"B": {"name": "Arithmetic Slip Trap", "explanation": "(16, 2): doesn't satisfy 5y = x since 5(2) = 10 ≠ 16. An arithmetic error in solving."}, "C": {"name": "Off-by-One Trap", "explanation": "(17, 1): plausible but 5(1) = 5 ≠ 17. Always verify BOTH equations."}, "D": {"name": "Trivial Trap", "explanation": "(18, 0): satisfies x + y = 18 but 5(0) = 0 ≠ 18. Always check the second equation too."}}
questions.patternTip: After solving a system, verify BOTH equations with your answer. D satisfies the first equation but fails the second—a classic trap for students who only check once.

questions.questionText: The point (8, 2) in the xy-plane is a solution to which of the following systems of inequalities?
questions.approach: Plug In (8, 2) directly. x = 8: positive. y = 2: positive. Look for 'x positive AND y positive.' That's choice A.
questions.whyRight: 8 > 0 and 2 > 0. Both conditions in choice A are met.
questions.trapAnalysis: {"B": {"name": "y Sign Flip Trap", "explanation": "y = 2 > 0, not < 0. Choice B requires y to be negative."}, "C": {"name": "x Sign Flip Trap", "explanation": "x = 8 > 0, not < 0. Choice C requires x to be negative."}, "D": {"name": "Both Wrong Trap", "explanation": "Neither x nor y is negative. This is the easiest elimination."}}
questions.patternTip: Systems of inequalities with a given point: just Plug In. Check x first (eliminates 2 choices), then check y (eliminates 1 more). No graphing needed.

questions.questionText: |x − 5| = 10. What is one possible solution to the given equation?
questions.approach: Two cases: (1) x − 5 = 10 → x = 15. (2) x − 5 = −10 → x = −5. The question asks for 'one possible solution'—enter either.
questions.trapAnalysis: {"One Case Trap": {"name": "One Case Trap", "explanation": "Forgetting the negative case and only finding x = 15. The SAT says 'one possible solution,' so either 15 or −5 is accepted."}, "Confusion Trap": {"name": "Confusion Trap", "explanation": "Entering 10 as the answer, confusing the right side of the equation with the solution."}}
questions.patternTip: |expression| = k always has TWO cases: expression = k AND expression = −k. The SAT asks for 'one possible solution'—enter either valid answer (15 or −5).

questions.questionText: The function f(x) = 7x + 1 gives the total number of people on a company retreat with x managers. What is the total number of people on a company retreat with 7 managers?
questions.trapAnalysis: {"Forget +1 Trap": {"name": "Forget +1 Trap", "explanation": "Reporting 49 after computing 7×7 but forgetting to add 1."}, "Order of Operations Trap": {"name": "Order of Operations Trap", "explanation": "Computing 7 + 1 = 8 then multiplying by 7 = 56 violates order of operations. Multiply first, then add."}}
questions.patternTip: Function evaluation: replace x with the given number everywhere. f(7) = 7(7) + 1. Multiplication first (order of operations), then addition.

questions.questionText: For h(x) = x² − 3, which table gives three values of x and their corresponding values of h(x)?
questions.approach: Calculate all three values: h(1) = 1−3 = −2. h(2) = 4−3 = 1. h(3) = 9−3 = 6. Find the table showing −2, 1, 6.
questions.whyRight: h(1)=−2, h(2)=1, h(3)=6. Only table B matches all three.
questions.trapAnalysis: {"A": {"name": "Add Instead of Subtract Trap", "explanation": "h(x) = 4, 5, 6 comes from x² + 3 instead of x² − 3. Sign error."}, "C": {"name": "Linear Trap", "explanation": "h(x) = −1, 1, 3 comes from treating h(x) = x − 3 (linear) instead of x² − 3 (quadratic). Forgetting to square x."}, "D": {"name": "Partial Correct Trap", "explanation": "D is correct for x=1 and x=2 but wrong for x=3: h(3) = 9−3 = 6, not 3. Students who don't compute all three values pick D."}}
questions.patternTip: Always evaluate ALL values before comparing tables. h(3) = 9−3 = 6 (not 3). The last entry in D is placed there to catch students who rush.

questions.questionText: The function f is defined by f(x) = 270(0.1)^x. What is the value of f(0)?
questions.approach: f(0) = 270(0.1)^0 = 270 × 1 = 270. The key fact: any nonzero base to the power 0 equals 1.
questions.whyRight: (0.1)^0 = 1. f(0) = 270 × 1 = 270. The coefficient 270 is the y-intercept of any exponential f(x) = a·bˣ.
questions.trapAnalysis: {"A": {"name": "Base-is-Zero Trap", "explanation": "0 would be correct if the base were 0. But 0.1 ≠ 0, so (0.1)^0 = 1, not 0."}, "B": {"name": "Zero-Power Only Trap", "explanation": "(0.1)^0 = 1 is correct, but the student forgets to multiply by 270. The answer is 270 × 1, not just 1."}, "C": {"name": "Evaluate at x=1 Trap", "explanation": "f(1) = 270 × 0.1 = 27. The question asks for f(0), not f(1)."}}
questions.patternTip: f(0) for exponential f(x) = a·bˣ always equals a (the leading coefficient), because b⁰ = 1. Instant shortcut: f(0) = 270.

questions.questionText: To estimate the proportion of a population with a certain characteristic, a random sample was selected. The estimated proportion is 0.49 with a margin of error of 0.04. Which of the following is the most appropriate conclusion?
questions.answerChoices: {"A": "It is plausible that the proportion is between 0.45 and 0.53.", "B": "It is plausible that the proportion is less than 0.45.", "C": "The proportion is exactly 0.49.", "D": "It is plausible that the proportion is greater than 0.53."}
questions.approach: Margin of error creates a range: estimate ± margin. 0.49 − 0.04 = 0.45 (lower bound). 0.49 + 0.04 = 0.53 (upper bound). The proportion plausibly falls within [0.45, 0.53].
questions.whyRight: The range [0.45, 0.53] captures all plausible values given the margin of error.
questions.trapAnalysis: {"B": {"name": "Below-Range Trap", "explanation": "Less than 0.45 is outside the margin of error. Ignores the lower boundary."}, "C": {"name": "Certainty Trap", "explanation": "'Exactly 0.49' ignores the margin of error entirely. The whole point of margin of error is that we're uncertain."}, "D": {"name": "Above-Range Trap", "explanation": "Greater than 0.53 exceeds the upper boundary of the margin of error range."}}
questions.patternTip: Margin of error = uncertainty range. Estimate ± margin = [lower, upper]. Values OUTSIDE this range are implausible. 'Exactly' is always wrong when a margin of error exists.

questions.questionText: A moving truck can tow a trailer if the combined weight of the trailer and the boxes it contains is no more than 4,600 pounds. What is the maximum number of boxes this truck can tow in a trailer with a weight of 500 pounds if each box weighs 120 pounds?
questions.approach: Set up: 500 + 120n ≤ 4,600 → 120n ≤ 4,100 → n ≤ 34.17. Since n must be a whole number and we need 'no more than,' round DOWN: n = 34.
questions.trapAnalysis: {"B": {"name": "Round-Up Trap", "explanation": "35 would exceed the limit. 34.17 rounds up to 35 mathematically, but in context 35 boxes violate the constraint. Always round DOWN for maximum capacity problems."}, "C": {"name": "No Trailer Weight Trap", "explanation": "4,600 ÷ 120 ≈ 38.3 → 38. This ignores the 500-pound trailer weight."}, "D": {"name": "Double Error Trap", "explanation": "Ignores trailer weight AND rounds up: 4,600 ÷ 120 ≈ 38.3 → 39."}}
questions.patternTip: 'No more than' = ≤. After dividing, ROUND DOWN for maximum boxes (rounding up would exceed the limit). Forgetting the trailer's 500 lb is the most common setup error.

questions.questionText: −4x² − 7x = −36. What is the positive solution to the given equation?
questions.whyRight: √625 = 25 (a perfect square!). Positive root: (−7 + 25)/8 = 18/8 = 9/4.
questions.trapAnalysis: {"A": {"name": "Wrong Discriminant Trap", "explanation": "7/4 comes from computing √(49 − 576) or making an algebra error in the discriminant. Note: discriminant = 49 + 576 (not minus)."}, "C": {"name": "Integer Guess Trap", "explanation": "Testing x = 4: −4(16) − 7(4) = −64 − 28 = −92 ≠ −36. Round numbers are placed as traps."}, "D": {"name": "Coefficient Trap", "explanation": "7 appears as a coefficient in the equation. Students guess it without computing."}}
questions.patternTip: The sign flip trick: multiply both sides by −1 first to make the leading coefficient positive. Then the discriminant is b² + 4ac (since c is now positive after the flip). Here: 49 + 576 = 625 = 25²—a perfect square.

questions.questionText: The table summarizes the distribution of color and shape for 100 tiles of equal area. Red tiles: Square=10, Pentagon=20, Total=30. If one of these tiles is selected at random, what is the probability of selecting a red tile? Express your answer as a decimal or fraction, not as a percent.
questions.approach: P(red) = (total red tiles) ÷ (total tiles) = 30 ÷ 100 = 3/10 or 0.3. Use the Total column for Red, not just one shape.
questions.whyRight: 30 red tiles (square + pentagon) out of 100 total. 30/100 = 3/10.
questions.trapAnalysis: {"Only Red Squares Trap": {"name": "Only Red Squares Trap", "explanation": "Using only red squares (10/100 = 0.1) instead of all red tiles (30/100)."}, "Wrong Denominator Trap": {"name": "Wrong Denominator Trap", "explanation": "Using 30/55 or 30/45 by dividing by a row total instead of the grand total (100)."}, "Percent Trap": {"name": "Percent Trap", "explanation": "Forgetting to express as a fraction/decimal and writing 30% instead."}}
questions.patternTip: Probability from two-way table: use the TOTAL row/column for your group, divided by the GRAND TOTAL. Red total = 30 (all shapes). Grand total = 100.

questions.questionText: For the given function f(x) = 2x + 3, the graph of y = f(x) in the xy-plane is parallel to line j. What is the slope of line j?
questions.approach: Parallel = same slope. y = 2x + 3 has slope 2. Line j has slope 2.
questions.whyRight: The coefficient of x in f(x) = 2x + 3 is 2. Parallel lines share slopes.
questions.trapAnalysis: {"Y-Intercept Trap": {"name": "Y-Intercept Trap", "explanation": "Reporting 3 (the y-intercept) instead of the slope."}, "Perpendicular Trap": {"name": "Perpendicular Trap", "explanation": "Reporting −1/2 (the perpendicular slope) instead of the parallel slope."}}
questions.patternTip: Parallel lines: identical slopes. Perpendicular lines: negative reciprocal slopes. 'Parallel to y = 2x + 3' → slope = 2. No calculation required.

questions.questionType: Word Problem: System of Two Equations
questions.questionText: A proposal for a new library was included on an election ballot. A radio show stated that 3 times as many people voted in favor of the proposal as voted against it. A social media post reported that 15,000 more people voted in favor than against. Based on these data, how many people voted against the proposal?
questions.approach: Let a = against. For = 3a. Difference = For − against = 3a − a = 2a = 15,000. a = 7,500.
questions.trapAnalysis: {"B": {"name": "Difference-as-Answer Trap", "explanation": "15,000 is the difference between for and against—not the number against. The question asks for 'against.'"}, "C": {"name": "For-Votes Trap", "explanation": "22,500 is the number who voted FOR. The question asks how many voted AGAINST."}, "D": {"name": "Multiply Trap", "explanation": "45,000 = 3 × 15,000. Incorrectly applying the ratio to the difference."}}
questions.patternTip: Two-relationship word problems: always define the variable as what the question ASKS FOR (votes against). Then express everything else in terms of that. 2a = 15,000 → a = 7,500.

questions.questionText: In the figure, lines m and n are parallel. If x = 6k + 13 and y = 8k − 29, where angles x° and y° are formed at line m by a transversal, and angle z° is formed at line n, what is the value of z?
questions.approach: Step 1: x = y (vertical angles) → k = 21. Step 2: x = 6(21)+13 = 139°. Step 3: z + x = 180° (supplementary) → z = 41°.
questions.trapAnalysis: {"A": {"name": "Arithmetic Error Trap", "explanation": "3 results from incorrectly solving for k (e.g., 2k = 6 instead of 2k = 42)."}, "B": {"name": "Stop-at-k Trap", "explanation": "21 is the value of k. The question asks for z. Students who find k and stop report this."}, "D": {"name": "Stop-at-x Trap", "explanation": "139° is the value of x. Students who find x but don't compute z = 180° − 139° report this."}}
questions.patternTip: Three-step trap: (1) find k = 21, (2) find x = 139°, (3) find z = 41°. The test puts k and x as answer choices. Always check: does the question ask for k, x, or z?

questions.questionText: In the equation −3x + 21px = 84, p is a constant and the equation has no solution. What is the value of p?
questions.approach: Factor: x(21p − 3) = 84. No solution requires: (coefficient of x) = 0 AND constant ≠ 0. Set 21p − 3 = 0: p = 1/7. Confirm: 84 ≠ 0 ✓.
questions.whyRight: 21(1/7) − 3 = 3 − 3 = 0. The equation becomes 0 = 84, which is false for all x.
questions.trapAnalysis: {"A": {"name": "Zero-p Trap", "explanation": "p = 0 gives −3x = 84 → x = −28. That's one solution, not no solution."}, "C": {"name": "Algebra Error Trap", "explanation": "4/3 comes from incorrectly setting up the no-solution condition (e.g., 21p = 4 instead of 21p = 3)."}, "D": {"name": "Right-Side Trap", "explanation": "p = 4 gives x(84 − 3) = 84 → x = 84/81, which is one solution."}}
questions.patternTip: No solution: coefficient of variable = 0 AND the resulting equation is false (constant ≠ 0). Factor first, then set the x-coefficient = 0. Don't set the constant = 0.

questions.questionText: The function f is defined by f(x) = (x − 10)(x + 13). For what value of x does f(x) reach its minimum?
questions.approach: Roots of f(x) = 0 are x = 10 and x = −13. Vertex x-coordinate = midpoint of roots = (10 + (−13))/2 = −3/2.
questions.whyRight: Average of roots: (10 − 13)/2 = −3/2. This is where the minimum occurs.
questions.trapAnalysis: {"A": {"name": "Product of Roots Trap", "explanation": "−130 = 10 × (−13). Multiplying the roots instead of averaging them."}, "B": {"name": "One Root Trap", "explanation": "−13 is one of the x-intercepts, not the x-coordinate of the vertex."}, "C": {"name": "Wrong Signs Trap", "explanation": "−23/2 = (−10 + (−13))/2. Student uses −10 (from the factor (x−10)) instead of +10 as the root."}}
questions.patternTip: Minimum of a quadratic from factored form = midpoint of the roots. Roots: x = 10 (from x−10=0) and x = −13 (from x+13=0). Average = (10−13)/2 = −3/2. No expanding needed.

questions.questionText: The function f(x) = (1/9)(x − 7)² + 3 gives a metal ball's height above the ground f(x), in inches, x seconds after it started moving on a track, where 0 ≤ x ≤ 10. Which of the following is the best interpretation of the vertex of the graph of y = f(x)?
questions.answerChoices: {"A": "The metal ball's minimum height was 3 inches above the ground.", "B": "The metal ball's minimum height was 7 inches above the ground.", "C": "The metal ball's height was 3 inches above the ground when it started moving.", "D": "The metal ball's height was 7 inches above the ground when it started moving."}
questions.approach: Vertex (7, 3): h = 7 (time in seconds), k = 3 (height in inches). Since a = 1/9 > 0, vertex is a MINIMUM. So minimum height = 3 inches.
questions.whyRight: Vertex (h, k) = (7, 3). a > 0 → minimum. The minimum height is k = 3 inches, occurring at t = 7 seconds.
questions.trapAnalysis: {"B": {"name": "Coordinate Swap Trap", "explanation": "7 is the TIME (x-value of vertex), not the height. Height is 3 (y-value of vertex)."}, "C": {"name": "x=0 Trap", "explanation": "'Started moving' means x = 0. f(0) = (1/9)(0−7)²+3 = 49/9+3 ≈ 8.4 inches, not 3. The vertex is at x = 7, not x = 0."}, "D": {"name": "Double Swap Trap", "explanation": "Both errors combined: using 7 as the height and interpreting the vertex as the starting point."}}
questions.patternTip: Vertex form (h, k): h is the x-input (time), k is the y-output (height). Since a > 0, the vertex is the MINIMUM. 'Minimum height' = k = 3. Not h = 7.

questions.questionText: In triangle JKL, cos(K) = 24/51 and angle J is a right angle. What is the value of cos(L)?
questions.approach: Right angle at J → K + L = 90° → L and K are complementary → cos(L) = sin(K). Find sin(K): adjacent = 24, hypotenuse = 51. Opposite = √(51² − 24²) = √2025 = 45. sin(K) = 45/51 = 15/17.
questions.trapAnalysis: {"Copy cos(K) Trap": {"name": "Copy cos(K) Trap", "explanation": "Reporting cos(K) = 24/51 as the answer for cos(L), not finding the complement."}, "Simplify Wrong Trap": {"name": "Simplify Wrong Trap", "explanation": "Simplifying 24/51 = 8/17 and reporting that as cos(L) without using the complementary relationship."}}
questions.patternTip: Complementary trig: in a right triangle, the two acute angles sum to 90°. cos(one angle) = sin(the other). cos(L) = sin(K). Use Pythagorean theorem to find the missing side.

questions.questionType: Quadratic: Discriminant for No Real Solution
questions.questionText: In the equation −x² + bx − 676 = 0, b is a positive integer and the equation has no real solution. What is the greatest possible value of b?
questions.approach: Flip signs: x² − bx + 676 = 0. Discriminant = b² − 4(676) = b² − 2704. For no real solution: b² < 2704. Since 52² = 2704 (discriminant = 0 → one real solution), b < 52. Greatest positive integer: b = 51.
questions.whyRight: 51² = 2601 < 2704 ✓ (no real solution). 52² = 2704 → discriminant = 0 → one real solution (not zero). So b = 51.
questions.trapAnalysis: {"b = 52 Trap": {"name": "b = 52 Trap", "explanation": "Answering 52—forgetting that discriminant = 0 gives exactly one real solution (not zero). The condition requires STRICTLY less than 0."}, "Sign Flip Trap": {"name": "Sign Flip Trap", "explanation": "Not flipping signs, leading to wrong discriminant setup."}}
questions.patternTip: No real solutions requires discriminant STRICTLY less than 0. Discriminant = 0 means exactly ONE real solution. So b must be strictly less than 52. The answer is 51, not 52.

questions.questionText: A graph shows two linear equations intersecting at one point. If a new graph of three linear equations is created by adding the equation x + 4y = −16, how many solutions (x, y) will the resulting system of three equations have?
questions.approach: The two graphed lines meet at their intersection. Check if that point satisfies x + 4y = −16. If not, the three-line system has zero common solutions.
questions.whyRight: The intersection of the first two lines doesn't lie on x + 4y = −16. No point satisfies all three equations at once.
questions.trapAnalysis: {"B": {"name": "Two-Line Thinking Trap", "explanation": "Two lines give exactly one intersection, but adding a third line that misses that point eliminates the common solution."}, "C": {"name": "Impossible Option Trap", "explanation": "A system of linear equations cannot have exactly two solutions. Zero, one, or infinitely many are the only options."}, "D": {"name": "Parallel Confusion Trap", "explanation": "Infinitely many would require all three lines to be the same line (coincident). They are not."}}
questions.patternTip: Three linear equations: if two lines meet at a point and the third doesn't pass through it, the answer is zero solutions. Two is never a valid answer for systems of linear equations.

questions.questionType: Exponential Function: Percent Decrease per Year
questions.questionText: The function f(x) = 5,470(0.64)^(x/12) gives the value, in dollars, of a certain piece of equipment after x months of use. If the value of the equipment decreases each year by p% of its value the preceding year, what is the value of p?
questions.approach: Per year means x = 12. The factor (0.64)^(12/12) = 0.64^1 = 0.64. Value retains 64% → decreases by 36%. So p = 36.
questions.whyRight: After 12 months, value = 0.64 × original. That's a 36% decrease.
questions.trapAnalysis: {"A": {"name": "Monthly Rate Trap", "explanation": "4 has no direct mathematical basis; comes from confusing monthly and yearly rates."}, "B": {"name": "Wrong Substitution Trap", "explanation": "5 may come from evaluating at x = 5 or another incorrect period."}, "D": {"name": "Remaining Value Trap", "explanation": "64% is what REMAINS after the decrease. The decrease is 100% − 64% = 36%. p = 36, not 64."}}
questions.patternTip: For per-year interpretation: substitute x = 12 (one year = 12 months). 0.64^1 = 0.64. The value is 64% of the original—so the DECREASE is 36%. Trap: D is 64% (what's left), not the decrease.

questions.questionType: Statistics: Effect of Adding a Constant
questions.questionText: A dot plot shows 15 values in data set A (range approximately 22–26). Data set B is created by adding 56 to each value in data set A. Which of the following correctly compares the medians and the ranges of data sets A and B?
questions.answerChoices: {"A": "The median of B = median of A, and the range of B = range of A.", "B": "The median of B = median of A, and the range of B > range of A.", "C": "The median of B > median of A, and the range of B = range of A.", "D": "The median of B > median of A, and the range of B > range of A."}
questions.approach: Adding a constant to every value: shifts median (and mean) by that constant, but does NOT change range or standard deviation. Median B = Median A + 56 > Median A. Range stays the same.
questions.whyRight: Median increases (by 56). Range = max − min = (max+56) − (min+56) = original range. Unchanged.
questions.trapAnalysis: {"A": {"name": "No-Shift Trap", "explanation": "The median does shift—it increases by 56. A constant shift always changes the median."}, "B": {"name": "Range Increases Trap", "explanation": "Range doesn't change when the same constant is added to every value. Both max and min increase by 56."}, "D": {"name": "Both-Increase Trap", "explanation": "Median increases (correct) but range stays the same (incorrect). D assumes range also increases."}}
questions.patternTip: Adding a constant k to all data: median shifts by k, mean shifts by k, range STAYS THE SAME. The spread (range, IQR, standard deviation) is never affected by uniform shifts.

questions.questionText: The equation x² + (y − 1)² = 49 represents circle A. Circle B is obtained by shifting circle A down 2 units in the xy-plane. Which of the following equations represents circle B?
questions.approach: Center of A: (0, 1). Shift down 2: new center = (0, −1). In circle equation (x−h)²+(y−k)²=r²: h=0, k=−1. Equation: x² + (y+1)² = 49.
questions.whyRight: Center shifts from (0,1) to (0,−1). In the equation: (y−(−1)) = (y+1). Result: x² + (y+1)² = 49.
questions.trapAnalysis: {"A": {"name": "Horizontal Shift Trap", "explanation": "(x−2)² shifts the circle LEFT 2, not down. Moving down affects the y-term, not the x-term."}, "B": {"name": "Up Instead of Down Trap", "explanation": "x² + (y−3)² has center (0, 3), which is 2 ABOVE center (0,1), not below."}, "C": {"name": "Horizontal Right Shift Trap", "explanation": "(x+2)² shifts the circle RIGHT 2. Horizontal shift, wrong direction, wrong axis."}}
questions.patternTip: Circle translations: shifting DOWN subtracts from the y-center. Center (0,1) down 2 → (0,−1). In the equation: (y − (−1)) = (y + 1). Many students pick B (shift up) or A/C (horizontal).

questions.questionType: Surface Area: Rectangular Prism in Context
questions.questionText: Two identical rectangular prisms, each with height 90 cm and a square base with side length s cm, each have a surface area of K cm². The two prisms are glued together along a square base to create a new solid whose surface area is (92/47)K cm². What is the side length, in cm, of each square base?
questions.approach: SA each = 2s² + 360s = K. Glued: remove 1 square base from each prism → new SA = 2K − 2s². Set equal: 2K − 2s² = (92/47)K → K × 2/47 = 2s² → K = 47s². Also K = 2s²+360s. So 47s² = 2s²+360s → 45s = 360 → s = 8.

questions.patternTip: When two solids are joined along a face, remove that face from BOTH (subtract 2 faces total from combined surface area). Set up K equation, then substitute. 360s = 45s² → s = 8.

questions.questionText: 210 is p% greater than 30. What is the value of p?
questions.approach: p% greater than 30 means: (increase / base) × 100. Base = 30. Increase = 210 − 30 = 180. p = (180/30) × 100 = 600.
questions.trapAnalysis: {"No Subtraction Trap": {"name": "No Subtraction Trap", "explanation": "Dividing 210/30 = 7 and reporting 700, forgetting to subtract 30 first to get the increase."}, "Forget ×100 Trap": {"name": "Forget ×100 Trap", "explanation": "Reporting 6 (correct ratio) but forgetting to multiply by 100."}, "Backwards Trap": {"name": "Backwards Trap", "explanation": "Dividing 30/210 × 100 ≈ 14.3% (backwards—puts base on top instead of bottom)."}}
questions.patternTip: Percent increase formula: (difference ÷ base) × 100. Base = the STARTING number (30). Difference = 210 − 30 = 180. 180/30 = 6. 6 × 100 = 600. Percent CAN exceed 100%—that's not an error.
